transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marcos Ruiz (Redwood), Alex Chen (Orion Eng Lead), Priya Kapoor (Orion Platform), Daniel Ortiz (Orion SRE), Maya Iqbal (Product), Jordan (Buyer)

Auto-summary (brief): New sampling run shows short seq fastpath wins for first-token latency but p95 spikes persist during ingress microbursts. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Lena (AE): okay hey everyone thanks for joining uhm, quick check — two changes to the pilot were pushed last night, Samir can you quick summarize?
[00:18] Samir (SE): yeah sure, so we toggled the fastpath kernel for sequences <= 64 and enabled a streaming window of 32 tokens for partial flushes. we also increased kv cache ttl to 300s for this run. small things but helps warm cache behavior.
[00:32] Alex (Orion): cool thanks, and just to be clear, our traffic has a lot of small auth messages, then occasional longer messages when we do reconciliation, so mix is heavy on short sequences but bursty.
[00:47] Priya (Orion): to add, the surge pattern is roughly 30–60s bursts every 10 minutes when batch job kicks in, so microbursts are real.
[01:05] Samir (SE): yep that's what the sampling showed. we ran a 24h microburst sampler — median TTFT for warm requests dropped from about 180ms to ~140ms on the fastpath, p50 improved, p95 still around 620ms in bursts.
[01:28] Maya (Product): sorry can you say p95 again? 620? that's above our SLA for auth flows.
[01:35] Samir (SE): yeah, 620ms p95 under microburst waveform. p99 further out at ~950ms but that's rare. these numbers are with our current provisioning and the fastpath kernel enabled.
[01:50] Daniel (SRE): are these numbers from your hosted run or our dedicated nodes?
[01:55] Samir (SE): these were on a small dedicated stack we mirrored — two nodes, measured end-to-end with ingress and egress. not cold-starts, mostly warm cache.
[02:08] Alex (Orion): what's the streaming handshake behavior? we saw some resets in last week's logs.
[02:14] Marcos (Redwood): good point — we observed a small increase in handshake latency when streaming window was very small (<=8) because of overhead per-chunk. bumping to 32 reduced overhead but increased tail in some cases due to delayed flush on very short sequences. there's a tradeoff.
[02:40] [crosstalk briefly] Jordan (Buyer): uh just to flag, if p95 is 620 that's not acceptable for checkout flows. any mitigations short term?
[02:50] Lena (AE): immediate mitigations — route critical auth paths to pinned capacity (reserved lane) and lower sequence window for those routes, also apply priority routing to keep them on fastpath kernels. we'll map which routes are critical.
[03:05] Alex (Orion): ok we can add a header to mark critical routes, how fast can we test?
[03:11] Samir (SE): we can run a validation tomorrow if you provide a 2h traffic sample or replay. Marcos will prepare the config.
[03:23] Priya (Orion): question — you mentioned KV cache TTL, how does that affect cold starts for the microbursts?
[03:30] Samir (SE): kv cache ttl basically keeps the cached embeddings/kv across requests for longer, so when bursts hit they see warm kv if within ttl. it doesn't help true cold starts, but reduces effective cold fraction across microbursts.
[03:45] Alex (Orion): understood. we do have a lot of short-lived sessions so TTL 300s seems safe to try.
[03:52] [00:04:00] Maya (Product): there's also cost concerns — fastpath uses more GPU cycles, is there an estimate of cost delta?
[04:10] Samir (SE): preliminary looks like 8–12% higher GPU utilization for fastpath vs quant-optimized kernel for the same throughput, but token efficiency and latency wins can offset some cost. we'll provide more exact numbers in the kernel comparison.
[04:28] Jordan (Buyer): do you support automatic fallback to cheaper kernel during low-priority windows?
[04:36] Marcos (Redwood): yes, runtime supports routing rules by priority and cost. we can route non-critical flows to quant kernel and keep critical on fastpath — this is a policy configuration.
[04:48] Alex (Orion): there was a note about path hedging in prior notes — is that still recommended?
[04:54] Samir (SE): hedging helps p95 but increases token duplication across two paths, so cost goes up. it's a knob if p95 is the top priority.
[05:06] [00:05:30] Daniel (SRE): about sample data — we cannot export PII, how much anonymization do you need?
[05:14] Lena (AE): we only need timing, length, and tokenized anonymized shapes plus headers for routing. no payloads. you can redact tokens and replace identifiers with stable pseudonyms.
[05:28] Alex (Orion): ok we'll prepare a 48-hour window anonymized, include 1% of detailed traces for deep p95 investigation.
[05:37] Priya (Orion): will you share the microburst sampling spreadsheet? the earlier link 404'd.
[05:42] Marcos (Redwood): sorry about that link — new link is shared in chat: https://redwood.internal/pilots/orion/microburst-sampling (placeholder). we'll also post a runbook.
[05:55] Samir (SE): quick note on kernel heuristics — currently we trigger fastpath when seq_len <=64 and KV cache warm. we can add extra heuristics like recent request density > X per second to avoid switching during sparse traffic.
[06:12] Alex (Orion): can that be per-route? some routes are high-frequency, others are not.
[06:17] Samir (SE): yes it's per-route. parallel tests we ran showed per-route heuristics improved stability.
[06:25] Maya (Product): any suggestion on provisioning for now? more nodes or smarter routing?
[06:31] Samir (SE): smarter routing + small reserved lane for auth flows is lower cost than doubling nodes. we'll validate.
[06:40] [00:07:20] Lena (AE): alright let's get into the new numbers — Samir you said you have a short table?
[06:46] Samir (SE): yep, numbers from the 24h run: baseline median TTFT 180ms, fastpath median 140ms, p95 baseline 700ms, p95 fastpath 620ms, p99 ~950ms. streaming handshake overhead reduced by ~30ms on average when window=32 vs window=8.
[07:06] Alex (Orion): useful — can we see the distribution by sequence length bucket?
[07:11] Samir (SE): yes we split buckets: <=32 tokens, 33-64, 65-200, >200. most requests are <=32, those get biggest win. >200 remain dominated by compute.
[07:26] Daniel (SRE): the reconciliation jobs that generate >200 tokens are batched during nightly windows — those we can route to lower-cost kernels.
[07:33] Priya (Orion): what about streaming partial responses for long sequences — did you observe any regressions?
[07:40] Marcos (Redwood): partial streaming for long sequences helps user-perceived latency but increases handshake overhead. for payment flows it's less important for long reconciliation jobs so we can favor throughput there.
[07:53] [00:08:30] Jordan (Buyer): are there any security or compliance impacts with the config changes?
[07:59] Lena (AE): no changes to data residency or retention. KV cache TTL change keeps data in cache longer but still in-memory on managed nodes; if you need enterprise isolation we can move to dedicated private deployment.
[08:14] Alex (Orion): we want to try a test where critical auth traffic goes to a pinned pool — how do we label that? header? path?
[08:22] Samir (SE): header X-Orion-Priority: high works. we can map that to a reserved model route and pinned instances.
[08:30] Maya (Product): what's the expected turnaround to see results after that change?
[08:34] Marcos (Redwood): we can push a policy change within a day and run a 2–4 hour validation. expect to see p95 improvements for those routes in that window.
[08:45] [00:09:10] Alex (Orion): question — you mentioned hedging earlier. let's quantify cost delta if we hedge 5% of requests.
[08:53] Samir (SE): rough math: hedged requests double tokens for those requests, so 5% hedging yields ~2.5% token increase overall. cost depends on token unit pricing but not huge for small hedge. we'll put exact calc in the spreadsheet.
[09:08] Lena (AE): ok we're approaching the last 20 mins, let's assign owners and timings.
[09:13] Marcos (Redwood): action: I'll post updated pilot config (streaming_window=32, kv_cache_ttl=300s) and a link to the kernel comparison run.
[09:22] Alex (Orion): we'll deliver anonymized traces by Tue 6/16 and mark critical routes headers.
[09:28] Daniel (SRE): will include a 1% detailed trace sample for 48 hours.
[09:33] Samir (SE): after we get traces we'll run a dedicated p95 focused benchmark with hedging toggles and two kernel configs — fastpath vs quant — and share results by 6/17.
[09:44] [00:10:30] Maya (Product): any blockers on Redwood side? infra or permissions?
[09:50] Lena (AE): no blockers; need your anonymized traces and permission to run dedicated comparison on the pilot dedicated nodes.
[09:58] Marcos (Redwood): we'll also test an intermediate kernel that uses lower precision to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
[10:06] Alex (Orion): one last ask: can you include a p95 remediation playbook so our oncall can apply short-term rules if spikes hit?
[10:13] Lena (AE): yes we'll draft a short runbook (3 bullets) and post to the shared drive.
[10:20] [00:11:00] Wrap-up and recap by Lena: agree on three deliverables: anonymized traces from Orion (by 6/16), Redwood kernel comparison (by 6/17), and updated pilot config + runbook (by 6/13). next sync scheduled tentative 6/18 to review run results.

Notes and artifacts referenced:
- microburst sampling spreadsheet (link posted in chat)
- kernel comparison runbook (will be posted)
- pilot config patch: streaming_window=32, kv_cache_ttl=300s, fastpath_threshold=64
- replay link placeholder: https://redwood.internal/pilots/orion/replays/2026-06-10

End transcript.
